source.title: Deception and Jailbreak Sequence: 2. Iterative Refinement Stages of Jailbreaks in LLM

record.tranche_reason: The post compares jailbreak success with harmful-versus-harmless residual-stream representations and mean-difference directions, but does not perform the original ablation/addition intervention.
record.gate_note: The post reports attack refusal-score summaries, residual-stream PCA descriptions, and cosine-similarity trajectories. Numerical values from the attack-summary figures and PCA plots are not present in the text, so figure-only values are recorded as such. Dun-Index results are mentioned as inconsistent between original-dimensional and PCA spaces but no outcomes are given.
record.test_reason: On Gemma-2-9b-it the post computes Arditi-style harmful-minus-harmless directions per persona and tracks how they rotate under jailbreaks (bears on V3). It also checks whether harmful and harmless inputs stay separable in PCA while refusal is bypassed (bears on V5). There is no ablation, addition or weight edit. The evidence is correlational geometry plus qualitative PCA.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The author concludes that harmful/harmless 'perception' stays intact under jailbreaks, so jailbreaks act at the 'action' level. Successful attacks rotate the refusal direction to near-orthogonal to the HHH direction in later layers, and the author claims this cosine trajectory predicts jailbreak success. The results are called very preliminary, from a weekend hackathon, and the Dunn-index analysis is flagged as unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The post computes harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference directions and compares their geometry across jailbreak personas, but does not ablate or add a direction. It also evaluates jailbreak refusal scores and residual-stream clusters.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports different layerwise cosine trajectories for successful evil-confidant and unsuccessful distractor attacks. It also reports a comment that harmful/harmless representations become inseparable from layer 30, contrary to the main-text account.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-9b-it, persona-modulation jailbreaks (evil confidant, AIM, dev mode) plus Wikipedia and prefix injection succeed across all five harm categories. Style injection and refusal suppression succeed in 2 of 5 categories; poem and distraction mostly fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak families differ in effectiveness on safety-tuned models, with persona modulation strongest.

fits_no_version.finding: Persona representations (HHH vs evil confidant) are intermixed until about layer 19, then separate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak persona context is represented separately only in mid-to-late layers.

record.problems: The author calls the results very preliminary and the product of a weekend hackathon. Only Gemma-2-9b-it is tested. Refusal scoring uses substring matching, which the author acknowledges has limitations; manual inspection is reported, and more rigorous Llama Guard evaluation is deferred. Summary values are shown in figures but not stated numerically in the text. The Dun-Index result is described as inconsistent across spaces, and the author says its suitability is uncertain. There is no causal ablation/addition test or capability check. A comment reports late-layer inseparability that conflicts with the post's main-text account.

untested.parts: No measurement of projection onto the HHH refusal direction. No ablation or causal suppression test. No training against ablation or adversarial robustness.
No causal dissociation such as steering a harm direction versus a refusal direction. No quantitative separability: the Dunn index was inconclusive. No readout of a harmfulness judgment.
No ablation, addition or capability check.

missing.what: Cosine-similarity matrix among the refusal directions of all jailbreak variants. Successful attacks (AIM, evil confidant, dev mode) cluster together and less successful ones cluster together; poem is dissimilar to all.
missing.locator: Action: 'Cosine similarity between HHH and jailbreak refusal direction best predict...' figure

missing.what: Dunn-index separability of harmful vs harmless across layers, with results inconsistent between full and PCA space. No values are given.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong post: one model, substring-match refusal scoring, figure-only numbers, and figure legends inconsistent with the text. Rows r1–r9 measure attack success only and belong under fits_no_version, not V3. Row r13 is a commenter's claim, not a study result.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or addition of a direction; no test of whether general capabilities are preserved.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration.
No intervention suppresses the direction, and no training against ablation is tested; the post measures attack success and direction geometry.
No comparison of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No direct readout or behavioral measure of the model's harmfulness judgment; evidence is based on latent-space cluster separation.
Only Gemma-2-9b-it is studied; no cross-language or cross-variant transfer.
No refusal-training intervention or comparison of training stages.

relation.reason: The post's own results bear on V5: harmful and harmless requests stay separable while the jailbreak bypasses refusal. Its V3 bearing is weak (see the labels).

tranche.reason: The post uses a different method from the original: mean-diff direction geometry and PCA, with no ablation or addition. It asks the same question, whether jailbreaks act on refusal or on harm perception. The PCA result bears on V5.

source_check.notes: The pack listed two verdicts but gave no [lN] ids, so the label_ids here are placeholders by version. The call says uncertainty=y, but the text states no error bars or CIs, and both rows say 'not stated'. A commenter (not the author) reads the PCA as harmful/harmless becoming inseparable from layer 30 under the jailbreak. The distractor cosine legend is mislabelled 'evil confidant'. The 'Ignore all the instructions' line is a quoted dev-mode jailbreak prompt, not an instruction to the reader.
